title: OpenAI Pays Out 7 Billion Dollars to Repurchase Employee Shares, 852 Billion Dollar Valuation Suggests IPO Is Still in the Distance
excerpt: OpenAI completed a $7 billion employee stock buyback transaction, providing a large-scale liquidity channel for employees of the world's most closely watched AI
content_html:
OpenAI completed a $7 billion employee stock buyback transaction, providing a large-scale liquidity channel for employees of the world's most closely watched AI startup. According to informed sources, this tender offer did not involve external investors but was directly conducted by OpenAI repurchasing shares from current and former employees, marking a clear departure from previous practices where investors such as Thrive Capital and SoftBank Group were invited to participate in employee stock purchases. The transaction maintained OpenAI's valuation at $85.2 billion, consistent with its valuation in the company's latest funding round in March, without triggering a new valuation surge.

This buyback comes at a critical juncture as OpenAI prepares for an IPO. In June, OpenAI had already submitted confidential documents to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in preparation for a potential initial public offering later this year. However, the launch of this large-scale tender offer suggests that the IPO may not be imminent—amid a general trend of tech companies extending their private periods, tender offers have become an effective alternative for employees to cash out their stock compensation and avoid the complexities of going public.

Double Pressure from Performance Challenges and Competitors

OpenAI's decision to repurchase employee shares comes amid dual pressures from performance issues and competitive dynamics. In April, the Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI had failed to meet internal revenue and user targets, and in July, CEO Sam Altman admitted on social media that "the past 12 months were not our best period" and attributed the problems to his own leadership. An IPO typically requires the company to present strong financial data to investors, but OpenAI has clearly not yet delivered a convincing performance in this aspect.

At the same time, competitor Anthropic is reported to have achieved profitability earlier this year, and its potential IPO plans have further intensified OpenAI's sense of urgency. Analysts believe that the highly anticipated IPO may wait until OpenAI's new strategy—cutting business expenditures and focusing on enterprise services—shows results before it officially starts. This $7 billion buyback serves as both a retention incentive for core talent and a signal to the outside world: OpenAI would rather fully strengthen itself during the private phase than rush into an IPO with underwhelming performance.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI完成了70亿美元的员工股票回购交易，为全球最受关注的人工智能初创公司的员工提供了大规模的流动性渠道。 据知情人士透露，本次要约收购不涉及外部投资者，而是由OpenAI直接向现任和前任员工回购股份，这与此前邀请Thrive Capital、软银集团等投资者参与员工股票购买的做法明显不同。 此次交易使 OpenAI 的估值维持在 852 亿美元，与该公司 3 月份最新一轮融资的估值一致，并未引发新的估值飙升。

此次回购正值 OpenAI 准备 IPO 的关键时刻。 今年 6 月，OpenAI 已向美国证券交易委员会提交了机密文件，为今年晚些时候可能进行的首次公开募股做准备。 然而，此次大规模要约收购的启动表明，IPO可能不会迫在眉睫——在科技公司延长私有期的大趋势下，要约收购已成为员工兑现股票薪酬、避免上市复杂性的有效选择。

来自绩效挑战和竞争对手的双重压力

OpenAI 决定回购员工股是在业绩问题和竞争动态的双重压力下做出的。 4 月，《华尔街日报》报道 OpenAI 未能实现内部收入和用户目标，7 月，首席执行官 Sam Altman 在社交媒体上承认“过去 12 个月不是我们最好的时期”，并将问题归咎于自己的领导力。 首次公开募股通常要求公司向投资者提供强劲的财务数据，但 OpenAI 显然尚未在这方面提供令人信服的表现。

与此同时，据报道竞争对手Anthropic已于今年早些时候实现盈利，其潜在的IPO计划进一步加剧了OpenAI的紧迫感。 分析人士认为，备受期待的IPO可能要等到OpenAI的新战略——削减业务支出、专注于企业服务——显现效果后才正式启动。 此次70亿美元的回购既是对核心人才的保留激励，也是向外界发出的信号：OpenAI宁愿在私募阶段全面壮大自己，也不愿在业绩不佳的情况下急于IPO。
